title_en: GTA 6 Player Spots What They Think Just Might Be Start of the Next Mount Chiliad Mystery
summary_en: GTA 6 player spots what they think may be the start of the next Mount Chiliad mystery.
body_en:
GTA 5’s most enduring mystery had players stumped for years. This long-running puzzle and Easter egg hunt revolved around a cryptic mural found inside the summit cable car station, and surrounding clues at the highest point of San Andreas.
The cable car station at the top of Mount Chiliad featured a cave drawing of a mountain topped by an Illuminati eye, with lines coming off the mountain connected to ancient alien-style carvings of a UFO, a cracked egg, and a jetpack. This mystery would later pay off in GTA Online, when The Doomsday Heist introduced an underground facility beneath Mount Chiliad, along with a flyable jetpack.
Now, fans exploring Leonida in GTA 6 have discovered some more strange markings, and some think it could be the start of the new game’s biggest mystery.
Redditor akspree posted what they think might just be GTA 6's version of the Mount Chiliad mystery. Now's the time for a big spoiler warning!
Really, don't read on if you want to avoid spoilers!
The markings are located on the Waink It scan, The Monument of Leonidan Supremacy, north of Port Gellhorn. The horse statues each have a metal sculpture on their head that looks like some kind of alien star chart.
One of the sculptures also has a traffic cone on its head, which is likely a reference to the equestrian statue of Field Marshal Arthur Wellesley located outside the Gallery of Modern Art, Glasgow. Rockstar North is a Scottish studio, so the traffic cone is likely just a nod to GTA 6’s heritage (and who can forget what Scotland fans got up to in the United States during the World Cup?!)
The base of the statue also features strange carvings, with stars and other geometric shapes etched into the stone. What these shapes mean is anyone’s guess, but they could even be simplified map locations, if someone can match the shapes up to the topography of the Leonida landscape.
If whatever this is follows the pattern established by GTA 5's Mount Chiliad, we might not find out what it means until whatever Rockstar is cooking up for GTA 6’s take on GTA Online to find out. Either way, hopefully it won’t take 10 years to uncover the secret this time around.
